chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: When the master of al-Ḥabashah set out with the cavalry, and with them was the elephant, to demolish the House, they passed by camels belonging to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and drove them away. That reached ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, so he came to the master of al-Ḥabashah. The doorkeeper entered and said, "This is ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim." He said, "And what does he want?" The interpreter said, "He has come concerning camels of his that they drove away, asking you to return them."

So the king of al-Ḥabashah said to his companions, "This is the chief of a people and their leader. I have come to his House, which he worships, to demolish it, while he asks me to release his camels! Had he asked me to refrain from demolishing it, I would have done so. Return his camels to him." Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to his interpreter, "What did the king say to you?" So he informed him, and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "I am the lord of the camels, and this House has a Lord who will protect it."

So his camels were returned to him, and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went back toward his home. On his way back he passed by the elephant and said to it, "O Maḥmūd." The elephant moved its head. He said to it, "Do you know why they brought you?" The elephant indicated with its head, "No." ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "They brought you to demolish the House of your Lord. Do you think you will do that?" It indicated with its head, "No." Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib returned to his home.

When morning came, they took it to enter the Sanctuary, but it refused and would not comply with them. Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to one of his retainers at that time, "Climb the mountain and look—do you see anything?" He said, "I see a darkness coming from the direction of the sea." He said to him, "Can your sight make it out completely?" He said, "No, but it is about to become clear." When it drew near, he said, "It is many birds, and I do not recognize them. Each bird carries in its beak a pebble like a small casting-stone, or smaller than a casting-stone."

Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "By the Lord of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, they want none but the people." Then when they came above their heads altogether, they cast the pebbles, and every pebble fell upon the top of a man’s head, passed out from his rear, and killed him. None of them escaped except one man who went to inform the people, but when he informed them, a pebble was cast upon him and killed him.

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْحَبَشَةِ: Abyssinia/Ethiopia, referring to the foreign ruler and his army
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْفِيلُ: the elephant brought with the invading army
key_terms.حَصَاةً: a small pebble cast by the birds upon the army
key_terms.رَبٌّ: Lord; here, Allah as the protector of the House

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the destruction of the army of the elephant and the protection of the Kaʿbah?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the episode of the People of the Elephant, describing how ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib entrusted the protection of the Kaʿbah to its Lord and how the invading army was destroyed by birds carrying pebbles. The report highlights divine protection of the Sacred House and serves as a historical account thematically connected to the Qur'anic account of Sūrat al-Fīl.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Humran, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the master of Ethiopia (Abraha) diverted with the cavalry horses and with them were the elephants, in order to demolish the House (Kabah), they passed by the camels of Abdul Muttalib. So they ushered them (for themselves). So (the news of) that reached Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> came to the master of Ethiopia (Abraha). So the proclaimer entered and said, ‘This is Abdul Muttalib<sup>asws</sup> Bin Hashim<sup>asws</sup>!’. So he said, ‘And what does he<sup>asws</sup> desire?’ The translator said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> has come regarding camels of his<sup>asws</sup> which have been ushered (by us), asking you to return them’.

So the king of Ethiopia said to his companions, ‘This is a chief of the people and their leader. I have come to his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> House which he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> worships, in order to demolish it, and he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> is asking me to free his<sup>asws</sup> camels? But, had he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> asked me to refrain from demolishing it, I would have done so. Return his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> camels to him’. So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said to his translator: ‘What did the king say to you?’ So he informed him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>. So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> am the lord of the camels, and for this House (Kabah), there is a Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, Protecting it’.

So he returned his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> camels to him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>, and Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> left towards his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> house. So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> passed by the elephant during his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> leaving, and he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said to the elephant: ‘O Mahmoud!’ So the elephant moved its head. So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said: ‘Do you know why they have come with you?’ So the elephant said with its head, ‘No’. So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said: ‘They came with you in order to demolish the House of your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>. Do you see yourself doing that?’ So it said with its head, ‘No’. So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> left to go to his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> house’.

So when it was morning, they went with it in order to demolish the Sanctuary. But it refused and prevented upon them. So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> said to one of his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> friends during that: ‘Ascend to the top of the mountain and look if you can see anything’. So he said, ‘I see blackness from the direction of the sea’. So he<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘Do you visualise all of it?’ So he said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘No, I can almost see it’. So when it was nearer, he said, ‘There are a lot of birds and I do not understand it. Every bird has a pebble in its beak like a flicking pebble, or smaller than a flicking pebble’.

So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said: ‘By the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>! They are not intending except for the group of people’. When they came to be above their heads, they cast the pebbles altogether, and every pebble fell on top of a man and exited from his behind, and killed him. So none escaped from them except for one man who (ran back to his hometown and) informed the people (what had happened to the king and his army). So when he had informed them, a pebble was thrown upon him, and killed him’.
en.sarwar: 24. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from ibn Mahbub from ibn al-Ri’ab from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj (and) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar all from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“‘Abd al-Muttalib will be resurrected as a whole nation (one ’Umma) with the grandeur of the kings and the complexion of the prophets. It is because he was the first one who believed in Bada’ (Allah’s revised will).

Once ‘Abd al-Muttalib sent the Messenger of Allah to the shepherds of his camels to help them with a runaway camel. He collected them all but had delayed to return home. ‘Abd al-Muttalib out of anxiety was holding the ring of the door of Ka‘ba. He kept saying, “O Lord, will destroy your own people.? If You would do so then it means that You have revised you decision.”

The Messenger of Allah came with camels and ‘Abd al-Muttalib had sent people to search him in all directions and valleys of (Makka). He would keep crying, “O Lord, will you destroy Your own people? If would do so then You may have revised Your decision.”
When saw the Messenger of Allah he held him to kiss and said, “Son, I will not sent thereafter for anything. I am afraid for you to be kidnapped and killed.”
